I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the cropping pattern I trust most: a winter wheat and summer maize rotation on most of my land. That fits our local climate, my age, my experience, and the way I already know how to manage water, fertilizer, and field work. At the start of the growing season, my wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so I will carry that through harvest with steady topdressing, watering when needed, and disease control if pressure shows up. After wheat harvest, I will quickly put in summer maize because it uses the heat and rainfall well and gives me stable grain output. If I keep a small extra piece more flexible, I will use it for peanuts in spring because it spreads risk, needs a bit less water than grain crops, and gives me some cash income. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I will not overcomplicate management. I will plough or rotary till where I need good seedbed conditions, keep fertilizer at practical levels, irrigate enough to protect yield, and spray only as much as I think is necessary to keep weeds, insects, and disease from cutting production.
